newsitem.title: UK: Lintas wins World Conservation's global ad account.
newsitem.headline: Lintas wins World Conservation's global ad account.

text.p: London-based advertising agency Ammirati Puris Lintas has been appointed to handle the World Conservation Union's (WCU) advertising account, worth an estimated one million pounds.
Lintas will be responsible for the WCU's global communications programme, including developing a new corporate logo and raising the organisation's profile to increase funding.
William Eccleshare, Lintas's chief executive, said the agency will also "help people to understand what must be done to achieve sustainable ecological development."
One of the agency's first tasks is to prepare for the WCU's 50th anniversary conference, which will take place next year in Fontainbleu, France.
Lintas won the account following a pitch against McCann-Erickson.

WCU was set up in 1948 to implement nature conservation programmes and to carry out scientific research. Its 900 members consist of government and non-governmental organisations including the Worldwide Fund for Nature and the Species Survival Commission.
